English: Assembly Narthex
A simple earthwork narthex, demarcated by wooden stakes and rough benches, serving as a provisional gathering space for early worship and council.
Wooden Gathering Hall
A modest timber hall where villagers and clergy assemble for religious rites, decorated with painted icons and basic altar furnishings.
Chamber of Rites
A dedicated space for the performance of sacred ceremonies, featuring stone floors and modest murals, accessible only to the initiated.
Stone Reception Hall
A stone-built hall with sturdy pillars and a raised dais, signifying the growing permanence and influence of the local faith.
Processional Chamber
A vast hall with colonnades and polished floors, designed for grand processions and prominent religious ceremonies, reinforcing the authority of the faith.
Decorated Nave
An expanded nave adorned with intricate carvings, painted frescoes, and relic alcoves, drawing pilgrims and enhancing the temples prestige.
Ornate Ceremony Hall
A resplendent hall with gilded altars, stained glass, and marble floors, hosting major festivals and assemblies that project the faiths wealth and learning.
Grand Nave
A monumental nave, its soaring arches and mosaics inspiring awe in all visitors. The center of theological debate and pilgrimage, symbolizing spiritual unity.
Sanctified Assembly Hall
A sanctified hall where the highest clergy convene, its relics and sanctuaries protected by ornate gates and guarded alcoves, radiating divine authority.
Majestic Ceremonial Hall
The pinnacle of spiritual architecture: a breathtaking hall with marble pillars, gold-inlaid walls, and monumental sanctuaries, attracting pilgrims and scholars from distant lands.
